body:
See [Notice of a Security Vulnerability](https://openid.net/notice-of-a-security-vulnerability/) for reference about a audience injection attack where an attacker (in this case a malicious AS) might trick a client into issuing a token with an audience claim conflicting with another AS (audience injection attack).

see CVE-2025-27370, CVE-2025-27371

This type of vulnerability might be applicable to other contexts.

Straw-man proposal intended to verify the lack of audience injection vulnerabilities:

> Verify that if a token issuer uses the same private key for issuing tokens to different audiences, the issued tokens contain an audience restriction that uniquely identifies the intended audiences in order to prevent a token to be reused with an unintended audience. If the audience identifier is dynamically provisioned, the token issuer must validate these audiences in order to make sure that they do not result in audience impersonation.

comments.body: The topic has been raised, and input/update for the proposal comes from Tim Würtele.

So is it a requirement into V52.2?

We also need to check that we don't overlap or duplicate V52.2.3:
> V52.2.3 Verify that the service only accepts tokens which are intended for use with that service (audience). For JWTs, this can be achieved by validating the 'aud' claim against an allowlist defined in the service.

Well, by this definition I think it is not a perfect match to V52.2 section, as it covers more the step "before using the token content", but not "how to build a token content".

> In any case, we are happy to provide examples/explanations as needed and to review proposed requirements - the one suggested by Elar above already went back and forth with us once.

Here I have been the "gateway" between you (@SECtim) and Gabrierl (@randomstuff). So I just try to use your know-how and organize a valid requirement to a valid section :)

Yes, I agree with @elarlang and @SECtim: if looks similar to 52.2.3 but is actually different because it is a requirement on the issuer whereas 52.2.3 is a requirement about the validator.

We currently mostly have requirements about token consumption/validation with the exception of 52.1.2 which covers both generation and validation.

Shall we have a section dedicated to token issuance?

If so, what shall we do with 52.1.2? Split it in two? Keep it?

Would we have additional requirements about token issuance?

> Shall we have a section dedicated to token issuance?

By principle, it could make sense, but at the moment, we don't have enough content for that.

If we have only one requirement for the potential new section, then I prefer to not go that we. In that case the best we can do at the moment is to fit the new requirement into one of those sections we already have and change the title and section text to widen the scope if needed.

If we have at least 2 requirements, then I have used the direction "the structure as a message" solution to send a clear message, in what precise step, scope, or context the requirement applies.

> If so, what shall we do with 52.1.2? Split it in two? Keep it?

Depends on the direction we choose.

> Would we have additional requirements about token issuance?

Probably it is a safe bet, that if we could have them, those could be already there.

@randomstuff - please try to brainstorm a bit the situation, if you split 52.1.2 into 2 requirements - one for building a token and another for validating a token. Then we can decide, how to handle the new proposed requirement and reorganize the section s to fit it.

So, let's brainstorm the "separate section" option
* V52.1 Creating token
  * Creating, building, generating - what fits here?
* V52.2 Token source and integrity
* V52.2 Using token content

Then we should have in V52.1 at the moment 2 requirements.
* Split from current 52.1.2
* new requirement from this issue, as currently worded in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2678#issue-2901569777

> If we have only one requirement for the potential new section, then I prefer to not go that we. In that case the best we can do at the moment is to fit the new requirement into one of those sections we already have and change the title and section text to widen the scope if needed.

Maybe we can change "V52.2 Using token content" into "V52.2 Token content" and include the proposed wording in this section?

> Maybe we can change "V52.2 Using token content" into "V52.2 Token content" and include the proposed wording in this section?

This is probably good solution do not over-structure it.

Can you prepare a proposal?

Proposed wording of the section text with expanded scope (straw-man proposition):

> This section describes requirements about the content of the token both for the issuer and for the consumer of the token in order to prevent unintended consumption of the token (eg. by the wrong service, for the wrong usage). Before making security decisions based on the content of a self-contained token, the consumer must validate that the token is intended to be consumed by this consumer and was issued for the purpose for which it was presented. On the other hand, the issuer must associate claims to the token in order to make this validation possible and ensure that a malicious actor may not deceive it into including malicious claims in the token.

Probably `eg.` should be `e.g.,`?

Update the related PR and assign/require @tghosth to review.
